question: Should OpenClaw adopt this new core durable-runtime control plane and its shared-state schema now, or keep durable orchestration within the existing TaskFlow/database-first ownership until a scoped architecture decision is accepted?
rationale: The branch adds a new persisted core runtime, public CLI/Gateway surface, and multiple operator environment controls; selecting its long-term owner and compatibility contract is a maintainer product and architecture choice, not a mechanical review repair.

options.title: Pause for architecture approval
options.body: Keep this implementation PR open but do not merge it until an owner approves the durable-core boundary and migration contract described by the related RFC.

options.title: Narrow to an isolated experiment
options.body: Retain only a fully opt-in, non-global experimental substrate with no shared-schema or public protocol commitment, then seek approval for a later integration slice.

options.title: Reject the new core runtime direction
options.body: Close the stack in favor of extending the existing TaskFlow/database-first owners rather than adding a parallel durable control plane.

recommendation.title: Pause for architecture approval
recommendation.body: Keep this implementation PR open but do not merge it until an owner approves the durable-core boundary and migration contract described by the related RFC.

likelyOwner.reason: The related RFC says a durable-work owner must decide the upstream architecture direction, while no concrete current-main owner is established in the supplied history.
